title: Dense ZZ modular full-rank certificate
objective: Accelerate public dense ZZ rank by certifying full row or column rank modulo a deterministic word-size prime through generated FLINT resources and falling back exactly for every inconclusive case

handoff.summary: Public dense ZZ rank now first reduces the borrowed generated FmpzMatrix resource modulo the fixed prime 46337. Maximal modular rank is a rigorous exact full-rank certificate; every smaller modular rank, including prime-collision cases, invokes the existing exact FLINT rank once. Explicit flint and linbox choices remain exact. On this host, a 200x300 random full-row-rank matrix measures about 4.9 ms through the certificate versus 2107 ms through exact FLINT, while a structured rank-199 matrix takes the expected 2203 ms modular-plus-exact fallback. The path never materializes host entries and emits distinct selection traces for certificate, inconclusive fallback, and explicitly exact execution.
risks: The fixed prime can be unlucky for a full-rank matrix; this is safe but invokes exact fallback, as proved by a diagonal entry equal to 46337.
Deficient matrices pay for one cheap modular reduction before their unavoidable exact FLINT rank computation.

Generated FmpzMatrix resources currently declare wasm=False, so browser support remains governed by the existing exact-matrix capability boundary. Native-disabled Node execution is differentially tested through the generated dynamic adapter.

The required portable tier reaches an unrelated checked-in website reference-data failure: its baseline has 21 unverified examples while test/website.cjs requires zero. The same 21 unverified examples are present in the integration checkout; all 132 other portable tests pass.
next_steps: Measure whether multiple deterministic primes are worthwhile for structured full-rank matrices that collide modulo 46337; never accept anything except maximal modular rank.
Apply the same one-sided certificate principle to other expensive exact predicates only where a modular witness is a proof, not a heuristic.
